messages:
maria: heads-up — over the last 10m I'm seeing a big spike in dropped pod connections in us-west2 GPU pool. Apps are seeing 502/504s and kube events show 'connection reset by peer'.
devendra: can you paste conntrack counters from affected node? `/proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count` and `/proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max`
maria: ran on gpu-node-17: `cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count` -> 65280; `cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max` -> 65536.
kyle: that's basically at full capacity. also check how many ESTABLISHED entries: `conntrack -L | grep ESTABLISHED | wc -l`
maria: `conntrack -L | grep ESTABLISHED | wc -l` -> 52103. a lot of them are to 10.0.0.0/16 (pod cidr) and 172.31.x.x (aws SNAT).
lisa: could be SNAT ephemeral port exhaustion rather than pure conntrack growth — long lived client connections + lots of ephemeral pairs. what's `ss -s` showing?
maria: `ss -s` shows high TCP time_wait and some retransmits. also see many retries in CNI logs.
tilly: any RDMA-enabled jobs on these nodes? RDMA flailing can produce lots of half-closed/established entries that stick.
maria: yes, a couple of inference jobs use RDMA path for cross-node KV cache. we just rolled a new workload template yesterday.
devendra: probable chain: RDMA retries -> high packet loss/fragmentation -> TCP retransmits -> many conntrack entries + long TIME_WAIT -> nf_conntrack fills. short-term: increase nf_conntrack_max and tune timeouts; medium: fix root cause (MTU/rdma config)
kyle: quick mitigation commands: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144` and `echo 262144 > /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max` (need sysctl persistence via node config). also `conntrack -F` will flush but it's destructive.
lisa: flushing breaks existing sessions (not great for prod). prefer cordon/evict the few worst nodes in the pool and drain, that will let conntrack tables reclaim gracefully.
ops-bot: deploy-bot noticed canary for inference-service-v2 started at 1978501300 and rolled back at 1978501452 (reason: 502 spikes).
maria: interesting — rollout overlaps with spike window. reverting might have dropped the transient rate but didn't fix table pressure.
devendra: check MTU mismatch: `ip link show` on the node and on the GNI/RDMA interface. fragmentation increases retries.
maria: `ip link show` -> eth0 mtu 1500, ib0 mtu 9000 (RDMA). looks like overlay (vxlan) packets get fragmented.
tilly: aha — overlay + jumbo + SNAT = fragmentation + retransmits. we should force consistent MTU on RDMA overlay or enable GSO/TSO offload correct for CNI.
kyle: action items: 1) short-term sysctl bump to 262k on nodes with >60% utilization, 2) cordon + drain 2 nodes to reclaim entries, 3) create nf_conntrack alert at 70% per-node; 4) roll back the inference canary if still running, 5) investigate CNI/MTU + RDMA mismatch.
lisa: I'll open a PR to our node-sshd/daemonset to set sysctl and add bootstrap test for net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max.
maria: I'll cordon gpu-node-17 and gpu-node-21 now and start drains.
devendra: also add a short-term conntrack timeout tweak: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=86400` -> maybe lower to free faster, but test.
ops-bot: alert: high-pod-disconnects us-west2-gpu-pool triggered at 1978501200 & resolved at 1978501860 (ticket INFRA-4721 created).
maria: thanks — filing notes in ticket: root cause suspected RDMA/MTU fragmentation causing retransmits -> conntrack pressure -> SNAT/ephemeral port pressure -> dropped connections. Will follow up with performance logs and CNI configs.
tilly: long-term: consider dedicated NAT gateway per node group or port-preserving SNAT for long-lived pod connections, and add a preflight that verifies consistent MTU across RDMA + overlay.
lisa: will add to infra roadmap. keep me posted if drains cause app regressions. :thumbsup:
maria: thanks all, updating INFRA-4721 with commands and next steps. will reopen if spike recurs.
